editorial:
Imagine starting a new job as a temporary teacher and having your worst nightmare come true on day one. You follow Honoka Kimijima into a quiet school during summer break, where the vibe is already kind of creepy. Everything goes south fast when a student jumps right off the roof in front of her. From there, the movie turns into a wild ride where sounds start playing a huge role in the scares. You will feel the tension build up as Honoka tries to figure out why this is happening and what the ghost actually wants. It is the kind of movie that makes you want to keep the lights on and your volume just right.

What really works here is the way the director uses sound to freak you out. The acting is solid, and the pacing keeps you on your toes without feeling too slow. While some of the jumps might feel a bit predictable, the overall mystery is enough to keep you glued to the screen. If you love J-horror, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie reveals that the ghost is tied to a cycle of grief and sound. Honoka discovers that the student's death was not a simple suicide but part of a larger, darker pattern. In the final scenes, the ghost attempts to pull Honoka into its world. It ends on a chilling note where you realize the curse is not fully gone, leaving you wondering if anyone is ever truly safe from the sounds of the dead.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves spooky J-horror and ghostly mysteries.
